findings.title: getBaseConditions returns unparenthesized SQL that breaks precedence when composed
findings.body: In two of the four branches, getBaseConditions returns authConditions or filterConditions as-is, without wrapping them in parentheses. Org and team auth conditions are top-level `(A) OR (B)` expressions, and the eventTypeId filter is also a top-level OR. Only the combined branch on line 73 wraps its parts. A caller that embeds this result next to other predicates, for example `WHERE ${base} AND status = ...`, gets SQL precedence `A OR (B AND status = ...)`. Rows that the org or team scope should exclude can then be returned. The fix is to wrap the returned fragment in parentheses in every branch so the method always yields one self-contained predicate.

findings.title: Public findMany was removed; scope enforcement is no longer automatic
findings.body: The public `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw SQL fragment. The old method applied the authorization and filter conditions as an AND on every query, so callers could not forget them. Callers now have to write their own `$queryRaw` and interpolate the fragment correctly. Nothing in this diff updates existing callers of `findMany`, so any remaining caller will fail to compile or will silently lose its scope restriction. Either keep a wrapper that always applies the conditions, or update all call sites in this PR.

findings.title: Constructor options type no longer enforces teamId for team scope
findings.body: The constructor's `options` parameter changed from the discriminated-union type `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the flat `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Code that passes `scope: 'team'` without `teamId` now type-checks. At runtime safeParse fails, `this.options` becomes null, and the service silently returns NOTHING (`1=0`) with no error. The compile-time check for team scope is lost. The constructor should keep the discriminated-union type.

findings.title: PR description says only tests changed, but the service is rewritten
findings.body: The description says the change only updates the integration tests and that the service was 'previously converted'. The diff rewrites the whole service: it removes findMany, adds getBaseConditions, changes SQL construction for org, team and filter conditions, changes the constructor option type, and changes isOrgOwnerOrAdmin. Reviewers following the description will not look at the service changes, which are the high-risk part. The description should list the service behavior changes.

findings.title: Caching tests were deleted without replacement
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block (cache authorization conditions, cache filter conditions) was removed and not replaced. The memoization in getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions still exists. The filter cache also stores null, which depends on the `=== undefined` check, and nothing covers that path now. The deletion is not mentioned in the PR description. The tests should be restored and adapted to Prisma.sql.

findings.title: Org and team scope SQL is only checked as strings, never executed
findings.body: The org and team scope tests compare the generated SQL template and parameter arrays for equality. Only the user scope is run against BookingTimeStatusDenormalized through $queryRaw. The AND/OR structure of the org and team conditions, which the PR description names as the high-risk part, is never executed. A wrong operator or a missing parenthesis would only show up in a live query. The tests should run org and team scope conditions against the view and assert which bookings are returned, including a booking from another team that must be excluded.
